what: Language recognition using the ‘textcat’ R package
title: Language Identification using the 'fastText' package (a Benchmark)
text: ‘textcat’ R package performs ‘text categorization based n-grams’. documentation package mentions: “… TextCat (https://www.let.rug.nl/vannoord/TextCat/) Perl implementation Cavnarand Trenkle ‘N-Gram-Based Text Categorization’ technique Gertjan van Noord subsequently integrated SpamAssassin. provides byte n-gram profiles 74 ‘languages’ (precisely, language/encoding combinations). C library reimplementation libtextcat adds one non-empty profile. ‘TC_byte_profiles’ provides byte profiles. ‘TC_char_profiles’ provides subset 56 character profiles obtained converting byte sequences UTF-8 strings possible. category ids unchanged original, give full (English) name language, optionally combined name encoding script. Note ‘scots’ indicates Scots, Germanic language variety historically spoken Lowland Scotland parts Ulster, distinguished Scottish Gaelic (named ‘scots_gaelic’ profiles), Celtic language variety spoken western Highlands Hebrides (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scots_language) …”  Apart previous 2 mentioned TC-profiles ECIMCI_profiles (26 profiles) also exists. benchmark ’ll use ‘TC_byte_profile’ (75 profiles) ‘TC_char_profiles’ (56 profiles) input textcat() function compute country names, default textcat() function returns. ’ll wrap function parallel::mclapply() observed returns results faster using multiple threads (benchmark used 8 threads).
